summary.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.
summary.overview: Management attributed the margin expansion to higher in-house capacity utilisation and a swing in JV performance from a loss of INR10 crore to a profit of INR3 crore YoY. Sales grew about 3% while value grew about 24%, with a few percent of sales lost in April when Morbi supply was shut for roughly 1.5 months. Price hikes of about 16-17% were passed through to the market, and gas costs rose 16-18% in the current period. Management guided to single-digit to mid-single-digit volume growth, maintained margins of 11%+, and announced a 9-plus million sq m South plant (about INR220 crore capex) due around end-Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Tiles (own plants and JVs)
segments.commentary: Standalone utilisation rose to 83% from 72%, with two lines under maintenance in the quarter. JV profit of INR3 crore vs a INR10 crore loss a year ago.

segments.name: Bathware / sanitaryware
segments.commentary: Management said Bathware margins run about 1% better than normal tile margins, and tile margins have now caught up. Bathware is growing healthily, with more sanitaryware balancing equipment planned.

segments.name: Construction chemicals (building materials)
segments.commentary: Large capacity added in the South, and a very large North capacity went on stream in July 2026; impact seen partly in Q1 and mostly in Q2.

segments.name: Somany Max
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR1.x crore from INR7 crore YoY. Management targets a loss of INR10 crore or less.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at single-digit to mid-single-digit for FY27; management says it will not promise high single-digit or low double-digit growth.
EBITDA margin of 11%+ maintained for the year, with an aspiration to reach 12% and above; management said it is trying to improve margins in Q3 and Q4 as balancing equipment comes on stream.
Balancing equipment and debottlenecking (about 3-4 million sq m, some reported as 4-5 million) to be largely done by end-Q3 and fully in place in Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.
Total capex to end-FY27 about INR275 crore (INR220 crore South plant plus balancing equipment), 65-70% funded by internal accruals; JV debt is non-recourse to Somany (60:40 JV).
9-plus million sq m South plant expected to add about INR350 crore revenue, ready in 12-15 months (end-Q3/start-Q4 FY28).
Management said maximum revenue at current capacity and prices is about INR3,700 crore; debottlenecking could add about INR300 crore partly by year-end.
Gas prices rose 16-18% in the current period; management said the company has passed through increases to date, and July and August gas prices are marginally higher.
capex_capacity: South plant: 9-plus million sq m greenfield, about INR220 crore outlay, operational around end-Q3 / start-Q4 FY28.
Balancing equipment in own plants and JVs (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) to add about 3-4 million sq m (also cited as 4-5 million) by Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.
Standalone utilisation at 83% in Q1 FY27 vs 72% a year ago; management expects slight further improvement in Q2.
Construction chemicals capacity added in South, and a very large North capacity commissioned in July 2026.
Bathware: additional balancing equipment planned at the sanitaryware plant.
demand_pricing: Price hike of about 16-17% taken in Q1 FY27; management said margins come from efficiency, with pricing being a pass-through.
Morbi was shut for about 1.5 months, with a 20-day ramp-up to full output from May. Management said about 15-17% of Morbi capacity has not restarted and will not restart.
Morbi exports are down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical issues and freight; this may persist until freight stabilises.
Channel inventory was built up in March ahead of the April shutdown, is now back to normal but lean, as dealers wait for gas-price cuts.
Retail project share is about 7-8% and government about 10-11%; management expects this to rise by 3-4 percentage points.
Management said July demand was affected by rain but sales were still pushed; it said demand was 'perfectly fine' overall.

Management said that in the Q1 volume growth shortfall versus the industry leader, the leader benefited from in-house Morbi production in polished vitrified tiles (PVT), which Somany is fully exposed to via outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and will it sustain from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to standalone utilisation rising to 83% from 72% and JV profit of INR3 crore vs a loss of INR10 crore YoY. It said margins are driven by efficiency rather than pricing and expects them to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Gas pricing across Morbi, North and South?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended natural gas cost is about INR68/unit. South and Morbi are around mid-INR70s (South partly on spot), and North is about INR68-69. Management did not give a blended fuel cost incl. biofuel.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth outlook and why guidance is only mid-single-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is currently mid-single-digit. It said the leader's higher growth came from in-house PVT production. It has been cautious after missed high-single-digit targets in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price premium over Morbi narrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Morbi raised prices by roughly double Somany's 16-17%, narrowing the gap. Morbi units are now on GEL gas, and their accounting is being rectified, which narrows landed-cost differences.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR275 crore to end-FY27 including the INR220 crore South plant and balancing equipment, with 65-70% from internal accruals. JV loan is without corporate guarantee from Somany.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2%-3% volume growth affected by outsourcing from Morbi, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Morbi outsourcing is not needed beyond a point because of freight. Own plants are targeted at 100% utilisation, with capacity located in North, South and West.

risks_watch: Gas cost volatility: blended natural gas about INR68/unit, with the current increase 16-18% and July/August prices marginally higher; management says the price pass-through has worked so far, but a gas-price cut could bring a price reduction.
Morbi supply restoration: 15-17% of Morbi capacity has not restarted and management says it will not restart; Morbi is back at 100% on GEL gas, so the price gap versus Morbi may keep narrowing.
Export weakness: Morbi exports down 50-60% from peak on geopolitical issues and freight, expected to persist until freight stabilises; watch for any domestic dumping.
Volume guidance: FY27 guided at single-digit to mid-single-digit; Q1 volume growth was about 3% and a 2-2.5% gap to the industry leader was attributed to the leader's in-house PVT production.

Execution: balancing equipment (3-4 million sq m, also cited as 4-5 million) due largely by end-Q3 FY27; South 9-plus million sq m plant (about INR220 crore) due end-Q3/start-Q4 FY28; JV margin swing (INR3 crore profit vs INR10 crore loss) and Somany Max loss target of INR10 crore or less.
key_quotes: So my margins really have not gone up because of pricing. My margins have gone up because of operational efficiency that we are producing 100% in our own plants and also our JV losses have come down.

Various people have promised, including us in the past that we'll have high single-digit growth, low double-digit growth, but never has been delivered. So we have been very, very cautious in what we are saying
Procuring from Morbi beyond the point becomes counterproductive because of freight.
No, 9 million square meters will only come in towards third quarter of next year. That is virtually a greenfield plant.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and standalone utilisation (83%), explicitly stating margins came from efficiency rather than pricing. Cautious on volume, declining to commit to high single-digit or low double-digit growth after past missed targets, and deflected the 18-19% leader margin comparison to offline discussion.
